prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1016; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision involving the insured's vehicle. The claimant reports neck pain and is represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Verified that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the loss date. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 3: Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact. Two other parties involved in the collision also place the claimant in the vehicle.

Entry 4: Scene photographs were reviewed and confirm several details of the impact. No independent witnesses have come forward to describe how the collision occurred.

Entry 5: Recorded statement taken from the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision happened matches what was given at first notice and in the earlier phone contact.

Entry 6: Medical records reviewed. The reported whiplash injury is consistent with the type and force of this crash. No prior injury to the same area of the body is known.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course of care and tapered as the claimant improved. Records show steady progress with no unusual gaps or escalations.

Entry 8: Repair estimate and inspection reviewed. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, but it is not yet clear whether all listed damage resulted from this impact, so a second review has been requested.

Entry 9: File is pending the second damage review and receipt of the final treatment summary. Reserve remains open and the claim will be reassessed once both items are received.
